events.objective: Establish the precise symptom onset and blast radius for settlement-service. Using query_logs and query_metrics, determine: (1) exact timestamp settlement throughput dropped to zero and when consumer lag began climbing, comparing to the ~08:22 report and to the config change time; (2) error signatures in settlement-service logs around onset (rebalance, CommitFailedException, max.poll.interval exceeded, DB timeouts, connection pool exhaustion); (3) whether lag growth is uniform or concentrated in specific partitions; (4) whether related services (ledger/posting, trade/order producer, broker) show concurrent error or latency anomalies. Report exact timestamps and error messages.

Enumerate everything that changed across ALL services in the window 07:30-08:30Z, not just settlement-service. Using get_deployments and get_config_changes, list each change with timestamp and service; identify the settlement-service consumer poll setting change specifically and any concurrent changes to upstream/downstream services. Then use get_service_dependencies to map settlement-service's upstream (message producer) and downstream (DB, ledger/posting, broker) dependencies, and search_historical_incidents for past 'stuck settlements' / consumer-lag incidents and their root causes.

Test whether settlement-service's dependencies are the bottleneck: using query_metrics (and logs if needed), check the health of settlement-service's downstream targets and message source for the window 07:30-09:59Z — DB connection pool saturation / query latency, ledger or posting service latency and error rate, broker metrics (partition rebalance count, under-replicated partitions, consumer group state), and producer publish rate for settlement messages. Determine whether any dependency shows degradation beginning at or before the lag onset, versus all dependencies looking healthy (which would point back to the consumer itself).

events.statement: Settlement throughput collapsed to zero inside the 07:40:00Z bucket: request_rate fell from a stable ~60-63 req/s (07:00-07:35) to avg 25.87 at 07:40 and avg 0.41 at 07:45, then stayed flat at ~0.40 req/s through 09:55 — i.e. zero real throughput persists for the whole window, ~42 min before the 08:22 report.

Consumer lag was flat/baseline (~39-50 msgs) through 07:35, then jumped in the same 07:40 bucket to avg 515.03 / max 1306.47, and climbed monotonically every 5-min bucket thereafter to avg 60220.76 at 09:55 (summary max 61605.53). Lag growth therefore begins at the 07:40 bucket, not at 08:22.
A config change was applied at 07:35:37Z (cfg-3004, consumer.max.poll.records=200) — ~4 min before the first error and the lag jump. It is the only config-change log line in the 07:30-08:30 window.

The earliest error is a deserialization failure, not a rebalance/commit/pool error: at 07:42:14Z "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)", repeated 213 times (first_seen 07:42:14Z). A second signature, "poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked", appears from 07:44:51Z with 196 occurrences.

All error signatures are pinned to a single partition: every one of the 40 earliest error lines references offset 'orders-3@8841207' (partition 3). No other partition id appears in the sample, and the log explicitly says 'partition blocked'.

Settlement-service shows no DB/connection-pool pressure and no HTTP 5xx spike: db_pool_in_use flat ~5.8-6.2 connections across 07:00-09:55, and error_rate flat ~0.17-0.27% throughout. A 'connection pool stats: healthy' INFO line appears at 07:53:07Z. So the failure is not pool exhaustion or DB timeouts.

events.answer: Settlement-service throughput dropped to zero in the 07:40:00Z 5-min bucket (request_rate ~60 req/s -> 0.41) and consumer lag simultaneously began climbing from a flat ~50 baseline to 1306 at 07:40 and 60,220 by 09:55 — i.e. onset is ~07:40, roughly 42 minutes BEFORE the 08:22 report and ~5 min AFTER a 07:35:37Z config change (cfg-3004, consumer.max.poll.records=200). The earliest error (07:42:14Z) is a schema mismatch, not an infra error: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', followed by 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt N), partition blocked' from 07:44:51Z. All observed errors are concentrated on partition orders-3 (offset 8841207), DB pool and HTTP error rate are flat/healthy, so lag growth is partition-local, not a global consumer failure.

Kafka exposes no partition-rebalance-count or consumer-group-state metric (only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions).

events.answer: No downstream dependency shows degradation at or before the lag onset: settlement-service db_pool_in_use is flat (~6 connections) and HTTP error_rate is flat (~0.2%), Kafka under_replicated_partitions is 0 throughout. The only dependency-side anomaly is a message-content problem — settlement-service first failed to deserialize orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2') at 07:42:14Z, after which it retries the same offset as a 'poison message ... partition blocked' and lag climbs monotonically from ~48 (07:30) to ~59k (09:50). This earliest signal precedes the reported 08:22Z onset and points at the consumed message/consumer schema handling rather than DB or broker saturation.

events.statement: The only config change across all services in the incident window was cfg-3004 on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records changed from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z by m.das ("Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes"). A wider 06:00-09:59Z query returned the same single change.

The only deployment in the window (and across 06:00-09:59Z) was dep-6010 on order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z, changing the OrderExecuted event schema: rename qty -> quantity, add venue, and a v2 event schema version header. Status 'live', not rolled back.
settlement-service consumes from kafka (queue-consume) and writes to ledger-db (db). Both kafka and ledger-db are marked shared=true, owned by platform.

order-service is the upstream producer into the shared kafka topic settlement-service consumes: order-service -> kafka (queue-produce), and order-service also writes to the same shared ledger-db (db edge).

Two historical incidents with matching 'settlements stuck / consumer lag growing' symptoms (HIST-112, HIST-104) had infrastructure_failure root causes from Kafka partition reassignment, not from config or schema changes. HIST-111 shows a past ledger-db slowdown affecting settlement-service. Stated by the tool as leads, not evidence about the current incident.

The two concurrent changes are ~5 minutes apart (cfg-3004 at 07:35:00Z, dep-6010 at 07:40:00Z), both shortly before the ~08:22Z report of a ~40-minute settlement gap. The order-service schema change (qty->quantity rename, new v2 header) alters the event format consumed by settlement-service on kafka, co-occurring with the settlement-service poll-batch reduction.

events.description: Did not inspect kafka broker/partition metrics or ledger-db telemetry for the 07:30-08:30Z window; no metric queries were run in this task (round 1 focus was change enumeration + dependency mapping).
Consumer error/deserialization logs on settlement-service were not retrieved.
No deployments/config changes exist for kafka or ledger-db platform components in the queried windows, so no admin-side change to shared infrastructure is visible.

events.answer: In the 07:30-08:30Z window exactly two changes occurred across all services: (1) cfg-3004 on settlement-service at 07:35:00Z reducing consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200, and (2) deployment dep-6010 of order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z introducing an OrderExecuted event schema change (field renamed qty->quantity, added venue, event schema version header v2). order-service is the Kafka producer that feeds settlement-service via kafka (queue-produce -> queue-consume); settlement-service also writes to shared ledger-db. The config change is the specific poll-setting change named in the report; the order-service event-schema deployment is a concurrent upstream change and a candidate for a consumer-side deserialization stall. Historical precedents (HIST-112, HIST-104) show similar lag symptoms previously caused by Kafka partition reassignment, not by schema or config changes -- leads only, not evidence here.

events.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change broke settlement-service deserialization on partition 3
cfg-3004 consumer.max.poll.records=200 reduction causes group instability / rebalances that stall processing
Kafka broker-side partition reassignment / infrastructure failure stalls the settlement consumer group
Downstream dependency (ledger-db) degradation blocks consumer mid-processing, lag grows independently of changes

Using query_logs and query_metrics, determine: (1) exact timestamp settlement throughput dropped to zero and when consumer lag began climbing, comparing to the ~08:22 report and to the config change time; (2) error signatures in settlement-service logs around onset (rebalance, CommitFailedException, max.poll.interval exceeded, DB timeouts, connection pool exhaustion); (3) whether lag growth is uniform or concentrated in specific partitions; (4) whether related services (ledger/posting, trade/order producer, broker) show concurrent error or latency anomalies. Report exact timestamps and error messages.
tasks.answer: Settlement-service throughput dropped to zero in the 07:40:00Z 5-min bucket (request_rate ~60 req/s -> 0.41) and consumer lag simultaneously began climbing from a flat ~50 baseline to 1306 at 07:40 and 60,220 by 09:55 — i.e. onset is ~07:40, roughly 42 minutes BEFORE the 08:22 report and ~5 min AFTER a 07:35:37Z config change (cfg-3004, consumer.max.poll.records=200). The earliest error (07:42:14Z) is a schema mismatch, not an infra error: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', followed by 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt N), partition blocked' from 07:44:51Z. All observed errors are concentrated on partition orders-3 (offset 8841207), DB pool and HTTP error rate are flat/healthy, so lag growth is partition-local, not a global consumer failure.

tasks.objective: Enumerate everything that changed across ALL services in the window 07:30-08:30Z, not just settlement-service. Using get_deployments and get_config_changes, list each change with timestamp and service; identify the settlement-service consumer poll setting change specifically and any concurrent changes to upstream/downstream services. Then use get_service_dependencies to map settlement-service's upstream (message producer) and downstream (DB, ledger/posting, broker) dependencies, and search_historical_incidents for past 'stuck settlements' / consumer-lag incidents and their root causes.
tasks.answer: In the 07:30-08:30Z window exactly two changes occurred across all services: (1) cfg-3004 on settlement-service at 07:35:00Z reducing consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200, and (2) deployment dep-6010 of order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z introducing an OrderExecuted event schema change (field renamed qty->quantity, added venue, event schema version header v2). order-service is the Kafka producer that feeds settlement-service via kafka (queue-produce -> queue-consume); settlement-service also writes to shared ledger-db. The config change is the specific poll-setting change named in the report; the order-service event-schema deployment is a concurrent upstream change and a candidate for a consumer-side deserialization stall. Historical precedents (HIST-112, HIST-104) show similar lag symptoms previously caused by Kafka partition reassignment, not by schema or config changes -- leads only, not evidence here.

tasks.answer: No downstream dependency shows degradation at or before the lag onset: settlement-service db_pool_in_use is flat (~6 connections) and HTTP error_rate is flat (~0.2%), Kafka under_replicated_partitions is 0 throughout. The only dependency-side anomaly is a message-content problem — settlement-service first failed to deserialize orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2') at 07:42:14Z, after which it retries the same offset as a 'poison message ... partition blocked' and lag climbs monotonically from ~48 (07:30) to ~59k (09:50). This earliest signal precedes the reported 08:22Z onset and points at the consumed message/consumer schema handling rather than DB or broker saturation.
